### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/extension-field-patch-targets.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8196881e7042f4e57543a6aaceffc1ab0ec89422`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/extension-field-patch-targets.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8196881e7042f4e57543a6aaceffc1ab0ec89422` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f2af38d5f0669e71e83ed10c835bac539d104efc` — the merge of head `d449a8b01233e6dfd69a337538693e21474fedcc` into base `8196881e7042f4e57543a6aaceffc1ab0ec89422`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f2af38d5f0669e71e83ed10c835bac539d104efc && git checkout f2af38d5f0669e71e83ed10c835bac539d104efc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8196881e7042f4e57543a6aaceffc1ab0ec89422 d449a8b01233e6dfd69a337538693e21474fedcc && git checkout -B drift-repro 8196881e7042f4e57543a6aaceffc1ab0ec89422 && git merge --no-ff d449a8b01233e6dfd69a337538693e21474fedcc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8196881e7042f4e57543a6aaceffc1ab0ec89422
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8196881e7042f4e57543a6aaceffc1ab0ec89422` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `60428213592b5e11492a8bbb85c6cbee85e9c4cf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/extension-field-patch-targets.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/field-patch-targets.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-object-extender-fold.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (the two hydration seams), docs/adr/0146-studio-designs-setup-administers-one-editor-per-item-paired-customize-package.md (D10), content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx, packages/objectql/src/registry-extension-field-patches.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-field-patch-targets.test.ts, .changeset/28733-field-patch-owner-fields-only.md

Inputs read: card #28733 (body and its four comments, the os-dev-report 6563103032 included), PR #28791 (body, file list, the net diff `d08b859a..60428213`, 8 files +238/-63, equal to GitHub's compare against `main`), and the check-runs on the head. Judged on the tree, never on the PR body's account of it.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Install door accept set, narrowed — right.** Step 2e of `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` now reads `registry.getFieldPatchTarget(name)` (the `own` contributor's stored definition) in place of `registry.getObject(name)` (the resolved object, every extender's fields folded in). A patch naming a field only another installed extension adds was admitted and is now refused, with the same `VALIDATION_ERROR` code, message and `details.refusals`. A target the same artifact delivers is still read off its body. Pinned in `marketplace-install-local-field-patch-targets.test.ts` with a real `SchemaRegistry` holding the owner plus an extension that adds `region`; the owner-field control beside it installs.
2. **Status of 2e, 400 to 422 — right, and not an accept-set change.** The refusal now answers `UNRUNNABLE_REFUSAL_CODE` / `UNRUNNABLE_REFUSAL_STATUS` (422), the pair 1c'' and the door's other body refusals answer (lines 1846, 1916 of the plugin at head). Card item 4 (comment 6561405801) asked exactly this; the test pin moved with it.
3. **Registry fold, narrowed — right.** `foldExtendersOntoDefinition` computes `ownFieldNamesOf(own contributor)` once; `applyFieldPatches` skips any patch whose field is not in that set, whatever the priorities, and `reportFieldPatchMisses` judges `ownFieldsTarget(merged, ownFields)` with the shared metadata-core judge, so what the fold names is what it skipped. `mergeObjectDefinitions` and `applyFieldPatches` are module-private (not exported), so their new parameter publishes nothing; the single call site passes it. The one external fold caller, `protocol-object-extender-fold.ts`, reaches the same code through `foldObjectExtendersOnto`, so the stored-row read, the by-name read and the code layer (`resolveOwnerLayer`, line 5663) agree.
4. **No-owner fold — right.** With no `own` contributor, nothing applies and nothing is named. This is the boot-ordering transient only: both hydration seams in `protocol.ts` (lines 18268, 29407) register a stored row as `own` when no packaged owner holds the name and as `overlay` otherwise, so every steady state has an owner, and `resolveObject` already serves nothing without one. Naming a transient miss would leave a once-per-registry warn that never retracts.
5. **Array-spelled bodies (ruling 3) — right.** The merge spreads `fields` as a record, so the fold now patches and judges the record spelling only; an array-spelled body handed to `foldObjectExtendersOnto` is not patched and the patch is named (was: not patched, not named). The metadata-core judge keeps reading both spellings for the two doors; its change is a docblock only. Pinned.
6. **`os validate` unchanged — right.** `cli/src/utils/field-patch-targets.ts` already composes the stack's declared `objects` across `packages[]` and judges against those; the three readers now answer the same for an extension-added field.
7. **Public surface, widened by one method.** `SchemaRegistry#getFieldPatchTarget(name)` is new on an exported class (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts` exports `SchemaRegistry`). Name-addressed through `resolveObjectKey` as `getObject` is; returns the contributor definition by reference, as `getObjectOwner` already does. See ② S1.
8. **Spec, prose only — right.** The `guidance.actions` sentence now lists `fields`, `label`, `pluralLabel`, `description`, `validations`, `indexes` carried and `fieldPatches` applied, and nothing else, which is the closed set `mergeObjectDefinitions` names at head (lines 667-686) and the set the manifest loop copies (`engine.ts` 9115-9126, plus `priority`, which orders and is not merged). No shape, key or refinement moves. No generated artifact embeds the sentence (`git grep` on the head finds the string in `object.zod.ts` alone), so `check:generated` has nothing to regenerate.
9. **`@objectstack/metadata-core` not in the changeset — right.** Its diff is a docblock.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/28733-field-patch-owner-fields-only.md`: `minor` on `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/spec`; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker; BREAKING banner, before/now, who sees it, the remedy. The PR body carries both declaration lines identically.
- **Level — right.** A value an author writes under `fieldPatches` is now refused at install (a value refused: `narrowed`), and the kind takes at least `minor` on every package the diff moves; the launch-window rule ships the narrowing as `minor`. The spec's share is prose, which keeps `minor` under the kind rule rather than `patch`.
- **Arm and disposition — right.** `(narrowing)` is declared, the banner is written, the ADR-0087 marker is one and well-formed; the migration count (0 in `examples/**` and `packages/*/src`) is stated.
- **S1 (should-fix) — the `Clause-②:` value under-declares.** The diff enlarges the public surface (judgment 7) while narrowing an accept set; `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` defines `yes (narrowing)` for exactly "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another", and the PR body itself calls the method "new public". Every gate-read fact (arm, kind, level, banner, disposition) is right, so the level does not move. Remedy: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset, naming `SchemaRegistry#getFieldPatchTarget`; or keep `no` by reading the owner through the existing public `getObjectOwner` and not adding a method.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared. None found.
- Card item 4 (status 422): done, test pin moved (①2).
- Dev out-of-scope 1 (the metadata-core miss sentence does not name the other extension): accepted as is; the sentence is true against the owner's declaration and its remedy already points at `fields`. No carrier needed.
- Dev out-of-scope 2 (option patches judged as merged in the fold, as declared at the door): escalated to ④ S2.
- Dev out-of-scope 3 (`packages/rest/src/meta-object-extension-property-classes.test.ts:31` quotes the retired sentence): ④ S3.
- Deviation 1 (metadata-core docblock edited outside the ruled surface): accepted; the docblock said the fold's target is the resolved object, which this diff made false; comment only, no changeset owed.
- Deviation 2 (no re-merge of `origin/main` after the gate run; head is 13 behind): noted; the check-runs on this head are the gate verdicts and the merge group reads them; nothing in this record depends on the 13 commits.
- Deviation 3 (probe runtimes stopped): no action.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up #28730` on the PR body: `skills/**` is untouched in the tree, as the claim ordered.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`** (the one `hits` file), judged against ADR-0146 D10 second rule, its describe sentence on `main`, and its first consumers (`mergeObjectDefinitions`, the manifest loop, the two doors):

- D10 says the extension may patch "a base field's display properties", with the patch applied by `mergeObjectDefinitions` after the additive merges; the `fieldPatches` describe sentence on `main` already says "the target object's own fields". The three readers now implement that sentence, so the published spec moves not at all and the code moves to it — the right direction for a narrowing, and the one the card's seat leaned to.
- The edited `actions` guidance is now true to the merge (①8) and to the comment above it. Tried to break it: `fieldGroups`, `hooks`, `listViews`, `membershipKeys` each have their own refusal sentence; nothing `mergeObjectDefinitions` carries is left unnamed, and `priority` is correctly not named as carried. Holds.
- The spec's own refusals are untouched: `refuseExtensionFieldPatchKeys` still refuses `__c` keys; the strict shape is unchanged; the membershipKeys test that reads a guidance string reads a different key.

**The cited code, read to judge the claim the sentence now makes ("applies `fieldPatches`"):**

- The fold: `ownFieldNamesOf` reads the owner's record-spelled `fields` and `ownFieldsTarget` rebuilds the merged object with only those names, so the apply step and the miss report cannot disagree; `tenantPatched` yields still apply on top. Two-priority test, same-extension test and array-spelling test pin the three card items. Holds.
- The door: `getFieldPatchTarget` returns `undefined` under exactly the condition `getObject` does (no `own` contributor), so `fieldPatchTargetRefusals` skips the same targets it skipped before; the fixed group (`workspace:*`) rules out a registry without the method. Holds.
- **S2 (should-fix) — two readings of "the owner's own fields" still split the readers, both pre-existing, both the card's family.** (a) Injected system columns: `registerObject` runs `applySystemFields` before contributor storage, so the owner's stored definition (what the fold and the door now read) carries `id`, `created_at`, the ownership columns; the stack declaration `os validate` reads does not. A patch of `created_at`'s label is applied and admitted, and refused by `os validate`, as before this diff. The new prose ("the owner's declaration", the mdx "a field the target does not declare") says otherwise. (b) An owner field an extension replaces through `fields`: the fold judges and patches its options as merged, the door and `os validate` as declared, as the dev named. Remedy: one sentence in the mdx bullet and in the `getFieldPatchTarget` docblock naming (a), a pin for (b) or a carrier card; or judge the door and the fold against the owner's declared fields before injection.
- **S3 (should-fix, prose) —** `packages/rest/src/meta-object-extension-property-classes.test.ts:31` quotes the retired `actions` sentence in a comment; the test's six-key table stays true. Reword in a prose rider.
- `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:5104` also says "`validations` and `indexes` only", about the idempotence subtraction, a different claim that is still true. Not stale.

**Check-runs on the head at the time of this read:** 36 success, 10 skipped (opt-in and scheduled lanes), 20 in progress (Test Core 3-6, Test UI 1-16 less two, Type Check UI, Type Check workspace), 0 failure, 0 cancelled. Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, every Lint lane, Type Check source and consumer gates, Build Core, Build Docs, Build and E2E UI and Test Core 1, 2, 7, 8 are green. Landing waits on the in-progress lanes as it always does; this record judges the tree.

Must-fix: none. Should-fix: S1, S2, S3.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d449a8b01233e6dfd69a337538693e21474fedcc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-field-patch-targets.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-object-extension-property-classes.test.ts, content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx, .changeset/28733-field-patch-owner-fields-only.md, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/extension-field-patch-targets.ts

This is a DELTA record over the PASS record on `60428213` (card comment 6563266243): it judges what moved between that head and this one, and carries forward what did not. The move is two commits: `ddabcf9a`, a merge of `origin/main` (`8196881e`), then `d449a8b0`, one commit answering the three should-fixes. Inputs: the PR body as the seat edited it, the file list, `git diff ddabcf9a..d449a8b0` (6 files, +23/-24), the net diff against `main` (9 files, +238/-64), the merge commit's combined diff on the PR's files, card #28733's comments since, card #28809, and the check-runs on this head. Judged on the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The merge carries no resolution hunks — confirmed.** `git show --cc ddabcf9a` over the nine PR files prints nothing: every PR file at the merge equals one parent or the other. The one file both sides moved, `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`, is #28746's `listedIdentity` hunk from `main` beside the PR's 2e hunk, non-adjacent, merged clean. The net diff against `main` is the PR's own nine files and nothing else.
2. **Public surface, no longer widened — right.** `SchemaRegistry#getFieldPatchTarget` is deleted; `git grep` on this head finds the name nowhere. `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` is untouched by the delta. The door now reads `registry.getObjectOwner(name)?.definition`.
3. **`getObjectOwner` returns the `own` contributor and nothing else — confirmed.** `registry.ts:5772`: a `find` over the contributors for `ownership === 'own'`; its docblock says an overlay is never returned, and ADR-0029 D9 keeps it meaning the table's owner. The fold reads the same `own` contributor through `ownFieldNamesOf`, so the door and the fold judge one body.
4. **The key-identity claim holds for every name that can fold — confirmed.** `computeFQN(_namespace, shortName)` returns `shortName` unchanged (`registry.ts:472`), and `registerObject` keys the contributor map by `computeFQN(namespace, schema.name)` through the one writer `openObjectEntry`, so the registry key IS the object's `name`. The name the door passes is `entry.extend`, and an extension registers under `computeFQN(undefined, extend)`, the same spelling, so any `extend` that reaches an owner in the fold reaches it at the door. The one divergence from the retired `resolveObjectKey` path is the legacy short-name hit: an object whose declared `name` carries `__` (the name regex `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$` allows it) is indexed under its tail, and `getObject('account')` would resolve `crm__account` while `getObjectOwner('account')` answers nothing. An extension spelled that way never folds onto that owner either (it registers under its own key, an orphan extender), so the door's not judging it changes no outcome. Not a finding.
5. **Door test — right.** The mock registry now exposes `getObjectOwner` backed by a real `SchemaRegistry`; the extension-added `region` refusal and the owner-field control stand as before.
6. **Changeset — right.** One line moved: the `Now` bullet names `SchemaRegistry#getObjectOwner` in place of the deleted method. Levels, arm, kind, banner and the ADR-0087 marker are byte-identical to the reviewed head.
7. **Everything else carries forward.** `registry.ts` apart from the deletion and one docblock paragraph, `object.zod.ts`, `metadata-core`, the registry test and the engine loop are unchanged from `60428213`; ① judgments 1 to 6, 8 and 9 of the PASS record stand.

### ② Semver level

- `minor` on `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/spec`; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; one well-formed `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker; BREAKING banner with before, now, who sees it and the remedy. PR body and changeset declare the same two lines.
- **S1 closed.** With `getFieldPatchTarget` gone the diff enlarges no public surface, so `no (narrowing)` is now the true answer to the Clause-② question; the arm and the kind were already right. Level unchanged.

### ③ Boundary flags

- S1 (public method under a `no` declaration): closed by deletion; the door reads the existing public `getObjectOwner` (①2-4).
- S2(a) (injected platform columns in the owner's stored declaration): named, behaviour unchanged, in three places — the mdx owner-only bullet, the door's `fieldPatchTargetRefusalsOf` docblock, and the `ownFieldNamesOf` docblock (which links `applySystemFields`, defined in the same file). The sentences are true to the code: `applySystemFields` runs on `own` and `overlay` bodies before contributor storage, so the fold and the door read the injected columns while `os validate` reads the authored stack. The mdx says "every object"; the plan withholds the family on some managed objects (#24314), a precision the lane seat may want, not a contract point.
- S2(b) (option patch on an owner field an extension takes over through `fields`): carried by card #28809 (open, 2026-11-01T21:12Z), titled exactly for the edge, with #28791 in its body. Not in this PR, as agreed.
- S3 (the rest test's quoted sentence): updated to the new sentence, with one clause saying `fieldPatches` is applied onto fields rather than carried, so the six-class table it pins stays whole. Correct.
- The seat's PR-body edit: `getObjectOwner` wording in the maintainer summary and the door bullet, a third acceptance note for S2(a), suite counts at `d449a8b0` (objectql 9961, cloud-connection 812), a dogfood re-run at this head. Matches the tree.
- `open_questions`: none. No new dev flags.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`** (the `hits` file): unchanged since `60428213`; the ④ judgment of the PASS record stands — the `actions` guidance names the closed set `mergeObjectDefinitions` carries and applies, the `fieldPatches` describe sentence on `main` is the rule all three readers now implement, and no generated artifact embeds the sentence.

**The cited code, re-read for the delta:**

- The door's target function is now one expression over a method that already existed, typed as `getObjectOwner?(fqn)` returning `{ definition? }`, undefined when no owner holds the name — the same skip condition `getObject` had, so `fieldPatchTargetRefusals` judges exactly the targets it judged before and refuses the extension-added field as pinned. Tried to break it with the legacy short-name path (①4): no reachable outcome moves. Holds.
- Deleting `getFieldPatchTarget` leaves the fold's `ownFieldNamesOf` as the only registry-side reader of the `own` contributor for patches, and the door's as the only external one, both through `ownership === 'own'`. No second copy of the lookup remains. Holds.
- The S2(a) docblock in `registry.ts` sits on `ownFieldNamesOf`, where the set is built, which is where a reader asking "why does `created_at` patch" lands. Right place.

Must-fix: none. Should-fix: none remaining; the three of the PASS record are closed (S1, S3) or carried (S2(b), #28809) with S2(a) named.

**Check-runs on this head:** 59 success, 10 skipped (opt-in and scheduled lanes), 0 in progress, 0 failure, 0 cancelled. Green: Test Core and all eight shards, Build Core, TypeScript Type Check with source, consumer, workspace, debt-ledger and UI lanes, Lint ESLint and every Lint lane, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness.

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** · `domain:server` seat 5 · `os-project-manager` · `session_01FEkQ5oc56xChD6Wrc4cGSt` · 2026-11-01T21:16Z · head `d449a8b0` · #28733

The maintainer's standing authorisation for landing reviewed PRs, verbatim: 「按照 pm-dispatch 规则复核过的都授权」.

席位意见:与 diff 相符。对象扩展的 `fieldPatches` 现在只能改所有者自己声明的字段：注册表合并、install-local 安装口和 `os validate` 三处给出同一个答案，安装口的这类拒绝从 400 改为与同门其它拒绝一致的 422。改别的扩展新增的字段以前会被安装口放行，现在被拒绝并指出位置。

1. **Shape:** draft against `main`, `Fixes #28733`, **minor** changeset with the BREAKING banner on `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/spec` (kind `narrowed`), ADR-0087 marker, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Skills-docs:` pointing at #28730. `check-governed-merges --pr 28791`: NOT governed, +238 / -64. `git merge-tree` against `main`: clean.
2. **Against the order:** ruling 1 → `ownFieldNamesOf` / `applyFieldPatches` / `reportFieldPatchMisses` in the fold judge against the `own` contributor, and step 2e reads `getObjectOwner(name)?.definition`; ruling 2 → `guidance.actions` prose in `object.zod.ts` true to `mergeObjectDefinitions`; ruling 3 → the fold patches and judges the record spelling only (measured: 230 bodies, 0 array); ruling 4 (card item 4) → 2e answers 422. Live probe: base admits the extension-added patch (200), head refuses 422 `VALIDATION_ERROR` with `details.refusals`.
3. **Accepted deviations:** a docblock-only edit in `metadata-core/extension-field-patch-targets.ts` that the change made false (no changeset entry, rightly).
